title: Research
text: My research asks how ambitious climate mitigation can be made feasible, equitable, and robust under real-world constraints.

title: Research
text:
Climate Policy & Integrated Assessment Modeling
I use integrated assessment models to examine interactions among energy systems, land use, the economy, and climate policy. My focus is not only on least-cost pathways, but also on what assumptions drive results and how scenarios can better support public decisions.
Questions: Which technology and policy choices determine mitigation outcomes? How robust are pathways across uncertain futures?

title: Research
text:
Carbon Pricing, Equity & Climate Finance
Climate policies distribute costs and benefits unevenly. This theme studies carbon-pricing design, regional and intergenerational equity, and financial mechanisms that can enable more ambitious mitigation.
Questions: How should mitigation costs be distributed? Which transfers or financing arrangements improve both fairness and feasibility?

title: Research
text:
Carbon Capture, Storage & Carbon Removal
CCS and CDR may be important for hard-to-abate emissions, but their potential is constrained by storage capacity, infrastructure, cost, governance, and public acceptance.
Questions: What role can international emission-trading mechanism play under storage constraints? When does reliance on CDR create unacceptable risks?

title: Research
text:
Long-term Decarbonization Pathways in Japan
This theme explores transitions toward and beyond net zero, with particular attention to Japan’s energy system and its relationship with global mitigation efforts.
Questions: How can Japan achieve net zero while maintaining energy security? What strategies are needed after net zero?

title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Research experience
Research Assistant, Kyoto University, 2025–present

Contributed the Japan Model Intercomparison Project on version 3 (JMIP3) by doing the AIM-Hub Japan model run and submitting the results to the IIASA database.
Contributed the development of AIM-Hub model by adding the new sector Ammonia, and also added related variables to the IAMC template and classified them with existed variables about Hydrogen.
Contributed developing Effort-Sharing Tool, a platform enabling linkage with AIM-Hub model. The tool redistributes global emissions and required carbon dioxide removal (CDR) based on fairness principles, using outputs from AIM-Hub.

Internship, National Institute for Environmental Studies (NIES), 2025.11 (two weeks)

As one of the members of AIM-Hub team, I was assigned to take a role of calculation and submission for the Japan’s long term emission target (JMIP).

Research Visit, International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), 2025.8 (one week)

Conducted the analysis of the relationship between various aerosol emissions from AIM-Hub and cooling effect calculated by MAGICC7. Its analysis results are implemented in AIM-Hub as a simple calculation.

title: About
text:
I am a climate and energy policy researcher interested in how societies can reach net-zero emissions fairly and feasibly. My work uses integrated assessment modeling and scenario analysis to connect long-term climate goals with near-term policy choices.
I am particularly interested in carbon pricing, climate finance, carbon capture and storage (CCS), carbon dioxide removal (CDR), and the design of decarbonization pathways for Japan and the wider world.
